question.text: Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, which of the following statements is true?
question.explanation:
From the graph, we see that

  • The slope of the tangent at $x=-4$ is negative, so $f'(-4) < 0.$

  • The slope of the tangent at $x=-2$ is positive, so $f'(-2) > 0.$

  • The slope of the tangent at $x=-1$ is zero, so $f'(-1)= 0.$

Therefore, $f'(-4) < f'(-1) < f'(-2).$

example.title: Comparing Slopes of Functions at Different Points

question.text: Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, which of the following statements is true?
question.explanation:
From the graph, we see that

  • The slope of the tangent at $x=-3$ is negative, so $f'(-3) < 0.$

  • The slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is positive, so $f'(1) > 0.$

  • The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is zero, so $f'(3)= 0.$

Therefore, $f'(-3) < f'(3) < f'(1).$

question.text: Find the values of $x$ for which the function $g(x)=x^3-12x+5$ is strictly decreasing.
question.explanation:
The function is strictly decreasing where $g'(x)<0.$ Differentiating $g(x),$ we get \begin{align*} g'(x)&=3x^2-12\\[5pt] &=3\bigl(x^2-4\bigr), \end{align*} so we need to solve the inequality \[ 3\bigl(x^2-4\bigr)<0. \]

The above inequality factors as \[ 3(x-2)(x+2)<0, \]

and the graph of $y=3(x-2)(x+2)$ has roots at $x=-2$ and $x=2,$ as shown below.

The graph is negative on the interval $\left(-2,2\right)$ between the roots, so we conclude that $g'(x)<0$ on the interval $\left(-2,2\right).$

Therefore, $g(x)$ is strictly decreasing on the interval $\Big( \bbox[5pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{{-2}}, \bbox[5pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2} \Big).$
